questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to try living very far away and being closer to nature and mountains

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Loved it

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. UC’s websites are way easier to navigate in than other universities i considered

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Lots of assistance at UC. I liked that a lot of UC’s assistance are in person in stead of online. When i arrived i went to a personal meeting with UC staff member, and they had a lot of intro meetings.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was very good

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Campus house and dorm rooms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I dont remember. I lived in a campus house where we cooked ourselves.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That there is lots of intro event for campus houses only, so its a nice way to meet people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I honestly were not very satisfied with Unilodge, because they put people with same nationalities, or even from the same home university in the same campus house. And i think the reason why most people go on exchange is to meet people from other nationalities and to challenge themselves. So i would recommend to text them before hand if you dont wanna stay with people from your own country.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was okay. I had lots of problems with my timetable that clashed. But because UC have in person meetings and drop ins, it is easy to get help to make it work.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I’ve got accepted in DK by UC, and applied for courses.
When i arrived at UC i went to a in person enrollment and was fully enrolled in the university, and got my student card.
School started and i changed courses a couple of times and finally got fully enrolled.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
In person help at the library or drop in sessions. 
There were also lots of other places to go for help likes student care.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was accepted for all of them. But changed a couple of times during the first two weeks of school.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Just apply for lots of courses on the pre-approval on your home university. 
There is a two week period in the beginning of school where it is possible to change courses without a fee. 
Just dont change too much, so you dont get way behind in classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very satisfied. I liked trying another university and UC have a good way of teaching about researching.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took some first and second year classes which were easy, but my third year classes was same level as at KU

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A bit different, because you get asses through the whole semester. A bit hard ti get assessed all the time but it made it easier at the final exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Antarctica: the cold continent
Antarctica and global change
Mountain, weather and climate
Coastal studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of them were very good. Coastal studies was a bit more difficult since it was a third year course.
They were all very interesting and relevant the present world.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Vegetables and cheese

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sooo many good clubs at UC.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Social clubs likes climbing club, tramping club, skiing club, curry club ect.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Maybe join a club. But half a year is not much if you wanna do everything so maybe choose only one.
I would definitely recommend to go on a lot of hikes (tramps) in the mountains. They have a pretty good hut system and lots of cool places to camp. Bring some camping gear if you have.
It is also cool to slender around in the city and the botanicals gardens in Christchurch.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
The mountains!!! Arthurs pas are not further away than 1-2 hours and have plenty of great hikes.
Also cool that UC has a three week break in the middle of the semester. A great opportunity to visit more of the country.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The locals are so cool!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Join clubs or register for a course with fields trips. I really enjoyed that.
And lot of the students in the classes dont know each other in the beginning so it is very easy to meet people in classes as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None. NZ has a very interesting culture but it is very easy to understand.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How much the maori culture is part of every system and way of teaching and thinking in New Zealand. Very interesting.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be open and join social events from the beginning
2. Go on tramps!!! Enjoy that you study in the most beautiful and cool country
3. Take courses with fields trips trips

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Nice to buy a car on markedplace so it is easier to get around. The intercity bus system are a bit bad and does only go to the cities, so it is very nice to have a car. 
I shared a small car with 3 others and that made it a bit cheaper. 

If you are in doubt of anything at the university just go to the library and ask for help.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think the most rewarding part was just to try studying and living in another country, and to meet so many interesting people from all over the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To study and live full time on English. But it got a lot easier.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
